title: A simple flash sintering setup under applied mechanical stress and controlled atmosphere
author: Caliman, Bichaud, et al.
materials: An interesting aspect of using a pellet sample instead of a dog-bone shaped sample is that the electrode material can be changed (changing the metallic ink layer between the ceramic and the platinum electrode) to ensure the electrical and electrochemistry compatibility between the electrode and sample material.

steps.title: Cold press pellets
steps.instruction: Uniaxially press powder at 60 MPa and isostatically at 250 MPa to obtain green pellets with relative density 50–55 % theoretical density; ensure flat surfaces for electrode contact.

steps.title: Apply metallic ink
steps.instruction: Coat both flat surfaces of each pellet with a thin layer of metallic ink to ensure intimate contact with platinum electrodes; optionally place platinum grids between ink layer and electrodes.

steps.title: Assemble electrode stack
steps.instruction: Place the ink‑coated pellet between two platinum disc electrodes connected to platinum wires; ensure the only electrical contacts are the electrodes.

steps.title: Configure furnace atmosphere
steps.instruction: Load the electrode‑sample assembly into the furnace; set the desired oxygen pressure (or other gas) using the atmosphere control system.

steps.title: Connect power source and software
steps.instruction: Connect the Pacific Smart Source 115ASX AC power generator to the electrode wires; launch UPC Manager V.1.4 software for control and data logging.

steps.title: Set electrical parameters
steps.instruction: Select signal nature (DC or AC) and frequency (0–1000 Hz); set voltage between 1 V and 120 V; set maximum current limit up to 15 A.

steps.title: Set temperature and pressure
steps.instruction: Heat the furnace to the target isothermal temperature (e.g., 900 °C); apply the desired mechanical pressure (smaller than SPS, as required for densification).

steps.title: Run flash sintering
steps.instruction: Start with voltage control; monitor current; when the preset current is reached, the system automatically switches to current control within 0.1 s.

steps.title: Current‑control mode actions
steps.instruction: In current‑control mode, either (a) discontinue power when the maximum current is reached, or (b) maintain a pre‑settled current for a defined dwell time.

steps.title: Data acquisition
steps.instruction: Continuously record voltage, current, and power versus time via the software.

steps.title: Post‑flash options
steps.instruction: Optionally maintain the current density for a set period after flash or interrupt the electric field to enable comparison of initial and final microstructures.

steps.title: Cool and retrieve sample
steps.instruction: Cool the furnace under the chosen atmosphere, then remove the sintered pellet for further characterization.
